standard_prerequisites: The algebraization theorem setting: f : X' to X corresponds to g : W to X_{/T}, with notation as in the chapter's general dilatation theorem
The valuative criterion for separatedness of algebraic spaces over a complete DVR, and its formal variant used for adic morphisms of formal algebraic spaces
Locality on the base for separatedness under etale base change, for morphisms of spaces and of formal algebraic spaces, and preservation of rig-surjectivity under base change
core_obligations: Forward direction: separatedness of f forces separatedness of g and rig-surjectivity of the diagonal, by the chapter's quasi-separated and diagonal lemmas
Etale-local reduction of the converse to X affine, using the three base-change locality lemmas
Valuative criterion: three cases for a map h from a complete DVR into X, according to whether it lands in U, in T, or has generic point outside T with closed point in T
Case III: form the adic morphism Spf(R) to the completed self fibre product, lift it along the rig-surjective diagonal, and algebraize the lift with the map-into-algebraic-space lemma
proof_roadmap: Prove the forward implication from the two cited lemmas
Reduce the converse to affines via etale descent and the already-established quasi-separatedness of f
Reduce separatedness to the DVR lifting property and dispatch Cases I and II (isomorphism over U; separatedness of W over Z)
In Case III lift the completed morphism along the rig-surjective diagonal and algebraize
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is a separatedness criterion for the algebraization f in terms of the formal model g and a rig-surjectivity condition on its diagonal (source lines 7197-7276, label lemma-output-separated). The solver must run an etale-descent reduction and then a three-case valuative argument whose essential case requires forming the completed self fibre product, recognizing the induced morphism as adic, lifting along the rig-surjective diagonal, and algebraizing; these steps are specific to the formal-algebraization toolkit and not routine. Allowed background: the chapter's dilatation theorem setting and the cited formal spaces lemmas, delivered as navigation pointers.
